en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape visible from many surrounding towns.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features massive limestone caves filled with observable stalactites and stalagmites.
The giant Rafflesia flower, which blooms in the forests of Bukidnon, can grow up to one meter wide.
Philippine tarsiers in Bohol have enormous, bulging eyes and elongated fingers that help them grip branches and catch insects at night.
The amihan season brings observable cool northeast winds that cause the leaves of many local trees to dry up and fall.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a visible body of water situated inside a crater on a small island within the lake itself.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are carved into steep mountain slopes, creating giant visible staircases from the valleys below.
The Philippine eagle, found in the forests of Mindanao, has a distinctive crest of long, dark brown feathers on its head.
The Verde Island Passage between Batangas and Mindoro is a deep, narrow strait characterized by visibly strong and turbulent ocean currents.
Callao Cave in Cagayan features a natural limestone chamber where bright sunlight visibly streams through a specific opening in the ceiling.
The Paoay Sand Dunes in Ilocos Norte feature massive, shifting hills of fine sand located directly adjacent to a coastal lagoon.
